name: ev-skills
description: EV team agent skills, each versioned on its own; `plugins` is generated by `skargo check`

plugins.name: excalidraw
plugins.description: Read, study or review an Excalidraw drawing (`.excalidraw`, `.excalidraw.json`, `.excalidraw.md`, excalidraw.com scenes): render it to PNG with a bundled renderer and look at it, cropped and zoomed per section. Use whenever excalidraw is mentioned, or a design board, whiteboard or sketch saved from it has to be understood, summarised, compared to code or redrawn.

plugins.name: readme-fw
plugins.description: How a repo's README.md is produced from docs/.readme_assets/. Read before editing any README.md or any file under docs/.readme_assets/ in a repo that consumes v_flakes' readme-fw.

plugins.name: skill-creation
plugins.description: Write, restructure, test or tune an agent skill (a SKILL.md and the files it links). Covers both a skill a repo ships about itself in `docs/skill/`, so agents in other repos can build against its library or framework, and a standalone skill that is its own source of truth: a workflow from the current conversation, a procedure, a domain. Use when asked to make, update, split, review or eval a skill, fix one that does not trigger, or make a project consumable by Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, opencode or other agents.

plugins.name: trading-data
plugins.description: Author and wire derivation graphs with the `trading_data` Rust framework — writing `#[node]` cells, spelling `type Deps`, declaring `graph!`, and driving it off `Replay` or `Live`. Use whenever a crate depends on `trading_data`, or a task mentions its primitives — `#[node]`, `graph!`, `Cell`, `Buffering`/`Folding`/`Sampling`/`Gating`, `Scans`/`Closes`/`Folds`/`Runs`/`Symbolic`/`Decides`/`Blind`, `Lanes`, `ReadClock`, `Replay`/`Live`.

plugins.name: v-flakes
plugins.description: Rules for working in ~/s/v_flakes (the shared Nix parts collection consumed by every other repo via `v_flakes.url = github:valeratrades/v_flakes?ref=v1.6`). Read BEFORE editing anything under ~/s/v_flakes, and before changing how any repo consumes v_flakes — covers how to release, what the pin policy is, and what re-exports exist. Also read before creating or labelling a GitHub issue in any v_flakes consumer: the label set and its lint come from here. Also read before editing any Cargo.toml: how a crate depends on another repo we own (local path overrides) is set here.
